about: Published worked examples of the measured-demand method for existing loads (NEC 220.87 and its predecessors). Only the numbers are kept; the articles are cited, not copied. Both print whole amps, so a match means our exact result rounds to each printed figure.

examples.source: Mike Holt, "Code Q&A: Calculating feeder or service loads," EC&M, August 8, 2014 (2011 NEC)
examples.note: The article rounds 98.58 A up to 99 A, then prints 99 × 125% as 123 A (exactly 123.75 A). From the published inputs the exact figures are 98.58 A, 123.23 A, 173.23 A, and 26.77 A spare.

examples.source: Charles R. Miller, "Branch-circuit, feeder and service calculations, Part LX," Electrical Contractor, February 15, 2011
examples.note: The article works in amps from a year of utility peak-demand data and gives no voltage; amps at 125% do not depend on the voltage chosen to express them in kW. Exactly: 928.75 A, 1,179.75 A, 20.25 A spare.
